=== sync-hermes-context.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sync-hermes-context.sh — one-way exact mirror of SRC into DST.
# A2: writes only to DST. A4: rsync -> fallback. A5/A7/A9: recursive exact
# mirror of {contents, dir structure, symlinks}. A6: --dry-run writes nothing.
set -u
set -o pipefail

SRC="${HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC:-/opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/}"
DST="${HERMES_CONTEXT_DST:-/workspace/hermes-context/}"
DRYRUN=0

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRYRUN=1 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

LOG_DIR="$HOME/.cache/hermes-context"
LOG_FILE="$LOG_DIR/sync.log"
COPIED=0
DELETED=0
MODE=rsync

log_summary() {
  # A6/A8: log append is a write — only on real runs, path outside DST.
  [ "$DRYRUN" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
  printf '%s mode=%s copied=%d deleted=%d exit=%d\n' \
    "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$1" "$COPIED" "$DELETED" "$2" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

die() {
  echo "sync-hermes-context: $*" >&2
  log_summary "$MODE" 1
  exit 1
}

[ -d "$SRC" ] || { MODE=n/a; die "source '$SRC' is not a directory"; }

# A8: never delete our own entrypoint; nothing inside DST may be an entrypoint.
ENTRYPOINT="$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || true)"
DST_REAL="$(readlink -f "$DST" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$ENTRYPOINT" ] && [ -n "$DST_REAL" ] && [ "${ENTRYPOINT#"$DST_REAL"/}" != "$ENTRYPOINT" ]; then
  die "entrypoint inside DST violates A8"
fi

MODE=rsync
if command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # contents-level sync: trailing slashes on both sides, no nesting (A4/Q4)
  if [ "$DRYRUN" -eq 1 ]; then
    if [ -d "$DST" ]; then
      rsync -a --delete --dry-run "$SRC"/ "$DST"/ || die "rsync dry-run failed"
    fi
    # DST absent under dry-run: nothing to compare, zero writes, exit 0 (A6)
  else
    mkdir -p "$DST"
    rsync -a --delete "$SRC"/ "$DST"/ || die "rsync failed"
  fi
else
  # A4 fallback: cp -a then recursive reconciliation at every depth.
  MODE=fallback
  if [ "$DRYRUN" -eq 1 ]; then
    : # no writes permitted under A6; verification below runs read-only
  else
    mkdir -p "$DST"
    cp -a "$SRC"/. "$DST"/ || die "cp failed"
    # delete stale entries at all depths: walk DST, remove paths absent from SRC
    while IFS= read -r rel; do
      if [ ! -e "$SRC/$rel" ] && [ ! -L "$SRC/$rel" ]; then
        rm -rf -- "$DST/$rel"
      fi
    done < <(cd "$DST" && find . -mindepth 1 -depth -print)
  fi
fi

if [ "$DRYRUN" -ne 1 ]; then
  # count what a real run produced (post-state vs SRC)
  TMP1="$(mktemp)"; TMP2="$(mktemp)"
  ( cd "$SRC" && find . ) | sort > "$TMP1"
  ( cd "$DST" && find . ) | sort > "$TMP2"
  COPIED=$(comm -23 "$TMP1" "$TMP2" | wc -l)
  DELETED=$(comm -13 "$TMP1" "$TMP2" | wc -l)
  rm -f "$TMP1" "$TMP2"
fi

# self_verify: recursive mirror_class check {contents, dir structure, symlinks}.
# Read-only, so safe under dry-run. Mismatch -> exit != 0 (never warn+0).
# Skipped entirely when DST does not exist yet (dry-run, nothing written: A6).
VERIFY_STATUS=0
verify() {
  local rel
  if [ ! -d "$DST" ]; then
    [ "$DRYRUN" -eq 1 ] && return 0
    return 1
  fi
  while IFS= read -r rel; do
    if [ ! -e "$DST/$rel" ] && [ ! -L "$DST/$rel" ]; then
      echo "missing in DST: $rel" >&2; VERIFY_STATUS=1
    elif [ -L "$SRC/$rel" ]; then
      [ "$(readlink "$SRC/$rel")" = "$(readlink "$DST/$rel")" ] || { echo "symlink mismatch: $rel" >&2; VERIFY_STATUS=1; }
    elif [ -d "$SRC/$rel" ]; then
      [ -d "$DST/$rel" ] || { echo "dir mismatch: $rel" >&2; VERIFY_STATUS=1; }
    else
      cmp -s "$SRC/$rel" "$DST/$rel" || { echo "content mismatch: $rel" >&2; VERIFY_STATUS=1; }
    fi
  done < <(cd "$SRC" && find . -mindepth 1)
  while IFS= read -r rel; do
    if [ ! -e "$SRC/$rel" ] && [ ! -L "$SRC/$rel" ]; then
      echo "stale in DST: $rel" >&2; VERIFY_STATUS=1
    fi
  done < <(cd "$DST" && find . -mindepth 1)
  return "$VERIFY_STATUS"
}

if ! verify; then
  die "mirror_class verification failed"
fi

log_summary "$MODE" 0
exit 0

=== README.md ===
# hermes-context sync

One-way recursive exact mirror: source `/opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/` → destination `/workspace/hermes-context/`. Both paths are env-overridable via `HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC` and `HERMES_CONTEXT_DST`. Writes go only to the destination (A2); source is read-only.

## Install

```sh
cp sync-hermes-context.sh ~/.local/bin/
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/sync-hermes-context.sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp hermes-context.service hermes-context.timer ~/.config/systemd/user/
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now hermes-context.timer
```

User-level units only — no root required. The script is standalone executable without systemd.

## Source-change workflow

1. Edit files under the source tree.
2. `~/.local/bin/sync-hermes-context.sh` to sync immediately, or wait for the 6-hourly timer.
3. Check `~/.cache/hermes-context/sync.log` for run summaries (timestamp, mode, copied/deleted counts, exit status).

## Dry-run test

```sh
~/.local/bin/sync-hermes-context.sh --dry-run
```

Under `--dry-run` zero bytes are written anywhere: no rsync/cp real run, no `mkdir`, no log append (A6). The verification pass is read-only and reports what would diverge. If the destination does not exist yet, the dry run still exits 0 — nothing has been written, so there is nothing to verify; a real run creates the destination and performs the full mirror.

## Sync strategy

- Recursive exact mirror of the mirror_class {file contents, dir structure recursive, symlinks} (A5/A7). Timestamps, metadata, and hardlink topology are out of scope (A9).
- rsync path: `rsync -a --delete` with trailing-slash contents semantics — destination end state equals source, never nested.
- Fallback path (rsync absent, A4): `cp -a` copy, then recursive reconciliation deleting stale entries at every depth, dirs included; symlinks mirrored as-is. Both branches converge to an identical end state (A5).
- Self-verification walks both trees recursively; any mismatch in contents, structure, or symlinks exits nonzero — never warn-and-exit-0.
- The log lives in `~/.cache/hermes-context/`, always outside the destination; the sync never deletes its own entrypoint (A8).
